skill.name: firebase-firestore
skill.description: Guides Cloud Firestore setup, security rules, indexes, SDK usage, and Firebase CLI workflows for Standard and Enterprise databases.
skill.summary: Plan, configure, and review Cloud Firestore databases with secure rules and index guidance.
skill.author: firebase

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives from Markdown examples, Firestore Rules syntax, or defensive security guidance. Five findings are confirmed because SKILL.md instructs agents to run Firebase CLI commands through npx, including metadata reads and database creation. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious intent.

remediation.issue: External Firebase CLI commands may run without enough confirmation.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running npx or firebase commands, and show the target project and database first.

remediation.issue: Database creation can mutate cloud resources.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm project, database ID, edition, location, and expected impact before creating or deploying Firestore resources.

remediation.issue: firebase-tools@latest can change behavior over time.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend a pinned or user-approved Firebase CLI version for reproducible workflows.

content.value_statement: Firestore projects need correct setup, indexes, SDK usage, and security rules. This skill guides database workflows and rule design for safer launches.
actual_capabilities: Identifies Standard and Enterprise Native Mode Firestore workflows.
Guides provisioning with Firebase CLI commands and configuration files.
Helps draft Firestore Security Rules with validation and ownership checks.
Explains SDK setup for web, Android, iOS, Flutter, and Python clients.
Documents index configuration for query performance and uniqueness.
Supports local emulator, rules deployment, and index deployment workflows.
limitations: Live operations require Firebase project access and authenticated CLI credentials.
Generated rules still need human review before production launch.
Current Firebase versions and regions should be verified from Firebase sources.
Enterprise pipeline examples depend on available SDK support in the project.

use_cases.title: Set Up a Firestore Backend
use_cases.description: Create the database plan, configuration files, emulator setup, and initial locked-down rules.

use_cases.title: Harden Security Rules
use_cases.description: Review collections, ownership rules, validation checks, and attack scenarios before release.

use_cases.title: Plan Query Indexes
use_cases.description: Map application queries to required single-field, composite, sparse, or unique indexes.

prompt_templates.title: Choose a Firestore Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me choose a Firestore database setup for my app. Ask what project, region, and client platforms I use.

prompt_templates.title: Add Client SDK Usage
prompt_templates.prompt: Guide me through adding Firestore to my app. Include the right SDK path, initialization steps, and safe query patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Draft Secure Rules
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze my Firestore collections and write prototype Security Rules. Include validation, ownership checks, and assumptions to review.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Rules and Indexes
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my Firestore rules and query patterns. Identify bypass risks, missing validations, and required indexes before deployment.

output_examples.input: I need Firestore for a new app.
output_examples.output: A setup plan with edition choice, location questions, initial configuration files, emulator steps, and deployment checks.

output_examples.input: My users collection stores public profiles and private emails.
output_examples.output: A recommendation to split public and private data, restrict owner-only reads, and validate all write fields.

output_examples.input: My app filters tasks by owner, status, and due date.
output_examples.output: An index plan that maps each query shape to required fields, ordering, and deployment steps.

best_practices: Confirm the Firebase project and database before running CLI commands.
Start rules with default deny and add only required permissions.
Validate creates and updates with the same domain-specific rule functions.
anti_patterns: Do not deploy generated rules without review and emulator testing.
Do not allow blanket authenticated reads on documents containing private data.
Do not use latest CLI commands for production changes without user approval.

faq.question: Can this skill create a Firestore database?
faq.answer: It can guide Firebase CLI creation workflows, but live changes require authenticated access and user approval.

faq.question: Does it support Enterprise Native Mode?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes separate guidance for Standard and Enterprise Native Mode Firestore databases.

faq.question: Can it write production-ready Security Rules?
faq.answer: It can draft strong prototype rules, but production rules need testing and human security review.

faq.question: Which client platforms are covered?
faq.answer: The references cover web, Android, iOS, Flutter, and Python usage patterns.

faq.question: Does it manage indexes?
faq.answer: Yes. It explains index files, query requirements, sparse indexes, and unique index behavior.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: Live Firebase CLI operations and version checks require network access to Firebase or npm services.
